s1.syndrome_frame: Malocclusion with tooth impaction and associated radiographic lesion
salient_findings: Radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region
key_facts: 22-year-old woman
Malaligned teeth
All permanent teeth erupted except third molars and lower left lateral incisor
Mild spacing between lower left central incisor and canine
Class II, Division 1 malocclusion
Crowding in maxillary anterior region
No history of prior dental extractions
Unerupted lower left lateral incisor with associated radiopaque lesion
Radiopaque lesion surrounded by thin radiolucent halo
Lesion obstructs eruption path of tooth

shortlist.label: Odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Radiopaque lesion associated with unerupted tooth, consistent with odontoma

shortlist.label: Compound odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple small radiopacities could represent compound odontoma

shortlist.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Radiolucent halo and association with unerupted tooth, consistent with adenomatoid odontogenic tumor

shortlist.label: Dens in dente
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic appearance of tooth within a tooth, consistent with dens in dente

shortlist.label: Complex odontoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large radiopaque lesion with potential for complex odontoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined radiopaque lesion surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, associated with an unerupted tooth, is consistent with an odontoma, which is a benign tumor composed of dental tissue that can obstruct tooth eruption.

rejected.label: Compound odontoma
rejected.why: While compound odontomas are also radiopaque lesions, they typically appear as multiple small tooth-like structures, which is not described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Adenomatoid odontogenic tumor
rejected.why: This tumor often presents with an unerupted tooth but typically has a more radiolucent appearance with internal radiopacities, not a well-defined radiopaque lesion.

rejected.label: Dens in dente
rejected.why: Dens in dente refers to a tooth with an invagination of the enamel, which does not match the description of a radiopaque lesion separate from the tooth.

rejected.label: Complex odontoma
rejected.why: Complex odontomas are also benign tumors of dental tissue but appear as a disorganized mass of enamel and dentin, not typically described as a well-defined radiopaque lesion with a thin radiolucent halo.
